# Write-Ahead Logging (WAL)

Write-ahead logging is a database durability mechanism that ensures data consistency even when the system crashes between operations.

## How WAL Works

The core principle is simple: **before applying any change to the main data pages, the database engine first appends that change to a sequential log file**. This two-step write process protects against data loss:

1. Change is written to the log (fast sequential write)
2. Change is later written to the main data pages (random I/O)

If a crash occurs between these two steps, the database can recover by replaying the log from the last checkpoint, restoring the system to its last consistent state.

## Trade-offs

### Benefit: Durability Without Full Flushes

WAL provides strong durability guarantees without requiring every transaction to force a full-page flush to disk. This is a significant performance gain compared to simpler durability models.

### Cost: Write Amplification

Every change is written twice:
1. Once to the log (sequential)
2. Once eventually to the main data pages (random I/O)

This small write amplification is an acceptable trade-off for the durability guarantee and the ability to batch page writes more efficiently.
